descriptions.Introduction to HTML: What HTML is and how browsers turn tags into a page. Everything on the web starts here.
descriptions.HTML Tag Basics: Learn opening, closing and self-closing tags and how elements nest inside each other.
descriptions.Basic HTML Page Skeleton: The boilerplate every page needs: doctype, html, head and body, and what each part does.
descriptions.Rules and Best Practices: Clean habits from day one: indentation, lowercase tags, proper nesting and comments.
descriptions.HTML Attributes: Attributes add extra information to tags, like links, ids, classes and image sources.
descriptions.Headings and Paragraphs: Structure your text with h1 to h6 and p so both readers and search engines understand it.
descriptions.Links and Media: Connect pages with anchors and add images, audio and video to your content.
descriptions.Text Formatting Tags: Emphasise or mark text using tags like strong, em, mark, sub and sup.
descriptions.Spacing and Separators: Control line breaks, horizontal rules and whitespace without hacking with spaces.
descriptions.Semantic Layout Tags: Use header, nav, main, section, article and footer so the page has meaning, not just boxes.
descriptions.Inside the Main Tag: How to organise the main content area with sections and articles correctly.
descriptions.Revisiting Anchor & Image Tags: Deeper use of links and images: relative vs absolute paths, alt text and targets.
descriptions.Div Tag (Block Elements): The generic block container used to group content for layout and styling.
descriptions.Span Tag (Inline Elements): The generic inline container for styling a small part of text. Know block vs inline.
descriptions.Lists in HTML: Ordered, unordered and description lists, including nested lists for menus.
descriptions.Tables in HTML: Show tabular data with rows, columns, headers and merged cells. Not for page layout.
descriptions.Forms and Inputs: Collect user data with form, input types, labels and buttons.
descriptions.Advanced Form Controls & Identifiers: Select, textarea, checkbox, radio, validation attributes and ids that link labels to inputs.
descriptions.Embedded Content: Embed videos, maps and other pages using iframe and related tags.

topics.description: Make pages usable for everyone, including people using screen readers or keyboards. It is also a hiring-interview favourite.
subtopics: Alt text and meaningful link text
ARIA roles and attributes (when and when not to use)

topics.description: Help search engines and social apps understand your page using the head section.
subtopics: Open Graph and Twitter card tags

topics.description: Built-in elements that replace old JavaScript hacks, saving time and code.

What does the viewport meta tag do?
Difference between a div button and a real button for accessibility.
practical: Add title, description, favicon and Open Graph tags to an existing page.
Build an FAQ accordion using only details and summary.
Create a modal using the dialog element.
Use picture and srcset to serve different images for mobile and desktop.

features: Fully semantic layout with correct heading order
Contact form with labels and validation attributes
SEO and Open Graph tags in head
FAQ section using details and summary
Passes a Lighthouse accessibility score above 90

descriptions.Introduction to CSS: CSS controls how HTML looks: colours, fonts, spacing and layout. Learn how a rule is written.
descriptions.Including Style: Inline, internal and external CSS, and why external stylesheets are the professional choice.
descriptions.Colors & Selectors: Pick elements with element, class and id selectors and colour them with names, hex, rgb and hsl.
descriptions.Text Properties: Style text with font, size, weight, spacing, alignment and decoration.
descriptions.Units in CSS: Absolute units like px compared with relative ones, and when to use each.
descriptions.The Box Model in CSS: Every element is a box of content, padding, border and margin. Understand it and layout stops being confusing.
descriptions.Border Properties: Style borders, round corners and create outlines and simple shapes.
descriptions.Padding and Margin: Space inside and outside elements, margin collapse and shorthand values.
descriptions.Display & Visibility: Block, inline, inline-block and none, and how hiding differs from removing.
descriptions.Alpha Channel (Opacity): Make colours and elements transparent with rgba, hsla and opacity.
descriptions.Relative Units: em, rem, %, vw and vh for layouts that scale with the screen and user settings.
descriptions.CSS Position Property: Static, relative, absolute, fixed and sticky: how elements are placed on the page.
descriptions.Z-Index & Background Details: Stack overlapping elements and control background images, size, repeat and position.
descriptions.Introduction to Flexbox: A one-dimensional layout system for rows or columns. The main tool for navbars and cards.
descriptions.Flex Container Properties: Control direction, wrapping and alignment from the parent container.
descriptions.Flex Item Properties: Control how individual children grow, shrink and align.
descriptions.Responsive Design with Media Queries: Change styles at different screen widths so one site works on phone, tablet and desktop.
descriptions.CSS Transitions: Smoothly animate property changes such as hover effects.
descriptions.CSS Transforms (2D & 3D): Move, rotate, scale and skew elements without affecting layout.
descriptions.CSS Animations & Keyframes: Create multi-step animations that run on their own using keyframes.

topics.description: A two-dimensional layout system for rows and columns together. Perfect for full page layouts and galleries.
subtopics: Grid vs Flexbox: when to use which

topics.description: Place items exactly where you want them, by line numbers or by named areas.
Build layouts that adapt by themselves using auto-fit and minmax.

theory: When would you choose Grid over Flexbox?
What does the fr unit do?
practical: Build a 3-column layout with header and footer using grid-template-areas.
Create a photo gallery where one image spans two columns.
Make a responsive card grid with repeat, auto-fit and minmax, with no media queries.
Recreate a dashboard layout (sidebar, topbar, content) with Grid.

topics.description: Target elements by their relationship to others or by their attributes.
subtopics: Descendant, child (>), adjacent (+) and sibling (~) selectors

Store colours and sizes once and reuse them everywhere. The base of every theme system.
Let CSS do the maths for fluid, flexible sizing.

What is the difference between ::before and :before usage with content?
Why use CSS variables instead of repeating values?
practical: Style a list so every odd item has a different background using :nth-child.
Create a custom tooltip using ::after and :hover.
Build a light/dark theme toggle powered by CSS variables.
Make a heading that scales smoothly between 24px and 48px using clamp().
Fix a stylesheet with conflicting rules using specificity, without !important.

topics.description: Design for the smallest screen first, then enhance. This is how real teams work.
Keep large stylesheets organised so teams can maintain them.
Know what the popular tools do and when to reach for them, after mastering plain CSS.

Pros, cons and when to use each

Refactor a messy stylesheet using BEM names.
Rebuild one card component in plain CSS, then in Tailwind or Bootstrap, and compare.
Add a global reset with border-box and test it.

newProjects.projectTitle: Responsive Admin Dashboard with Dark Mode

Theme switch powered by CSS variables
Hover and focus effects with pseudo-classes

descriptions.Introduction to JavaScript: What JavaScript is, where it runs and how to add it to a page. It makes websites interactive.
descriptions.Variables and Rules: Named containers for data, with the naming rules and conventions to follow.
descriptions.Variable Declaration (let, const, var): How let, const and var differ in scope and reassignment, and why modern code avoids var.
descriptions.Data Types: Numbers, strings, booleans, null, undefined, objects and the typeof operator.
descriptions.Comments in JS: Explain your code with single-line and multi-line comments.
descriptions.Operators in JS: Arithmetic, comparison, logical and assignment operators, plus == vs ===.
descriptions.Conditional Statements: Make decisions with if, else, switch and the ternary operator.
descriptions.Loops in JS: Repeat work with for, while and do-while, and control them with break and continue.
descriptions.Strings in JS: How text is stored, indexed and compared in JavaScript.
descriptions.Template Literals: Backtick strings with embedded expressions and multi-line support.
descriptions.String Methods in JS: Built-in tools to search, slice, replace and transform text.
descriptions.Arrays in JS: Ordered lists of values and how to create, read and update them.
descriptions.Looping over an Array: Different ways to go through every item: for, for...of and forEach.
descriptions.Basic Array Methods: Add, remove and find items with push, pop, shift, unshift, indexOf and includes.
descriptions.Advanced Array Methods: Slice, splice, sort, reverse and joining arrays together.
descriptions.Functions in JS: Reusable blocks of code with parameters and return values.
descriptions.Arrow Functions: A shorter function syntax and how it handles this differently.
descriptions.Callbacks & forEach Loop: Passing a function into another function. The first step to functional style.
descriptions.Higher-Order Array Methods: map, filter and reduce transform data without manual loops. Used everywhere in real projects.
descriptions.Web Dev Basics & The Window Object: How the browser is structured and the window object that holds everything.
descriptions.Understanding the DOM: The browser's tree version of your HTML that JavaScript can read and change.
descriptions.DOM Manipulation: Selecting Elements: Find elements with getElementById and querySelector.
descriptions.DOM Manipulation: Properties: Read and change text, HTML and values using textContent, innerHTML and value.
descriptions.Attributes and Styling: Change attributes, classes and inline styles from JavaScript.
descriptions.Inserting and Deleting Elements: Create, add and remove elements to build dynamic pages.
descriptions.Introduction to Events: Events are actions like clicks and key presses that your code can respond to.
descriptions.Event Handling in JS: Connect functions to events using inline and property handlers.
descriptions.The Event Object: The object passed to handlers with details like target, key and coordinates.
descriptions.Event Listeners: addEventListener, removing listeners, bubbling and event delegation.
descriptions.Prototypes in JS: How objects inherit from other objects behind the scenes.
descriptions.Classes and Objects: Blueprints for creating many objects with shared behaviour.
descriptions.Constructors: Special methods that set up a new object when it is created.
descriptions.Inheritance: Reuse and extend a class by creating a child class.
descriptions.The 'super' Keyword: Call the parent class constructor and methods from a child class.
descriptions.Error Handling (try-catch): Handle failures gracefully with try, catch, finally and throw.
descriptions.Synchronous vs Asynchronous: How JavaScript runs one thing at a time and handles waiting tasks.
descriptions.Timers & Execution Context: setTimeout, setInterval and the call stack and event loop behind them.
descriptions.Callbacks & Callback Hell: Why nested callbacks become unreadable and what to use instead.
descriptions.Promises: Objects that represent a future result, with then, catch and Promise.all.
descriptions.Async-Await & IIFE: Write asynchronous code that reads like normal code, plus immediately invoked functions.
descriptions.Working with APIs (Fetch & JSON): Get data from servers using fetch and read it as JSON. The base of every real app.
descriptions.Browser Storage: Save data in the browser with localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies.

practical: Create a counter using a closure with private state.
